I've seen some good articles, sure, but this… this is just SO COOL.

An anomaly that grows backwards in time? That's just fantastic.

It makes total sense that the foundation never realized what was happening, as their memories were continually being overwritten as the initial size "grew".

The ending was especially eerie. Huge +1, amazing work.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: It's not the most likely candidate, but the effects of removing England from history would be so far-reaching predicting the plausibility of different alternate histories would be meaningless (especially as English as a global lingua franca is heavily influenced by the USA, which would be completely unrecognisable in this situation). I don't think Japan would rise to global domination, but I could easily envision a world where there is no commonly accepted global language, and Japanese would be highly influential - without the USA, Japan is the world's second largest economy, so I don't see why the Foundation-equivalent's main branch couldn't be there. I could easily suspend my disbelief here for artistic yields, anyway.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Perhaps it would be fitting out-of-universe, but given that Japanese is only spoken natively on one chain of islands that purposely kept itself isolated from the rest of the world for centuries, it wouldn't make sense for it to become a lingua franca for the world if English never existed, nor would it be likely that the SCP Foundation's main branch would be in Japan.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Sadly it's a punch conditional on a few terms (Japan is an archipelago, and its official language is neither English nor conditional for English to exist). You could rewrite this and change the location and whatnot (destruction of England-the-country and a switch to Spanish to Portuguese, or something), but in my opinion that would be just disrespectful to the author and the community that created one of my top 5 favorite articles.

Also, since the Foundation is not aware of how the phenomenon actually works, from their perspective they're reducing an event horizon the size of the Moon down to a sphere of 0.7 radius almost instantly. That's the best containment procedure they've ever had! Of course they will redouble the efforts.

Albeit, of course, since the Moon-sized event horizon was there for long enough, one raises the question of why even try to contain it, since it's now the definition of normalcy, as in, enormous anomalies just be like that sometimes.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: It's an event horizon that appears to shrink by feeding it stuff, but what actually happens is it remains the same size today but becomes larger retroactively. The original article was initially written in Japanese, then gradually switched to English because Japan the country has never existed.

Oh, and if you didn't wait around to the end, go back and run it again.
